Subject: LLM data handling: training, retention, and evidence

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this. Our security and privacy teams have a short list of items we need to verify for our vendor review ahead of procurement:

- Do you use customer prompts or responses to train or improve your base or fine-tuned models by default? If yes, please describe the scope and opt-out mechanisms.
- What are your default retention windows for prompts, responses, and associated logs (access, trace, KV cache metadata)?
- Are there contractual controls (DPA/SCCs) or technical options for immediate deletion of a customer’s data on request?
- Can you provide SOC 2 Type II evidence or a SIG/CAIQ summary that addresses data segregation and training controls?
- Any DPIA or AI-specific privacy assessments you can share for regulated workloads?

If possible, please send a short written response and any summary artifacts (PDFs) we can attach to our compliance questionnaire. We’re on a tight timeline — procurement needs this by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Anna

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. I’ll summarize answers below and attach the relevant artifacts. Marcus and Evelyn are helping compile the SOC 2 and DPIA summaries.

High-level answers:
- Training on customer prompts/responses: By default, we do not train customer data into our shared model weights. Customer-provided content is used for inference only unless an explicit, documented opt-in for model improvement is agreed in the contract. For Dedicated and Private deployments, customers can elect isolation where no training telemetry leaves their environment.

- Retention windows: Default retention for prompts/responses and request/response logs is 30 days. Metadata and access logs that are necessary for billing and abuse monitoring are retained for 90 days by default, configurable by enterprise contract.

- Deletion & contractual controls: We offer a standard DPA (includes SCCs language) and support contract clauses for accelerated deletion (48-72 hour SLA for bulk deletion) for enterprise customers. We also provide a data deletion API for programmatic requests.

- Evidence: Attached (1) Redwood_Data_Retention_v1.2.pdf, (2) Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf, (3) DPIA_AI_Processing_Summary.pdf.

I’ll follow up after Marcus confirms the SIG rows you flagged during intake.

Best,
Soojin

Hi Anna — thanks for the patience. Please find our consolidated responses below and the requested summary artifacts attached. If you need any additional SOC 2 detail or the completed SIG questionnaire, we can provide redacted rows or schedule a deeper walkthrough.

Itemized responses (short):
1) Training on customer content:
   - Default behavior: Customer prompts and responses are used solely for inference and are NOT incorporated into shared model training.
   - Opt-in: Model improvement using customer data requires an explicit contract amendment and documented opt-in process. We keep audit logs for any such opt-ins.
   - Dedicated / Private: For Dedicated and Private deployment customers, telemetry and inference traces remain in-customer or within the reserved capacity and are not used for shared-model training.

2) Retention and logs:
   - Prompts/responses retention (default): 30 days.
   - Audit/access logs & billing metadata (default): 90 days.
   - Configurability: Retention windows are configurable in the enterprise contract and can be shortened on request.

3) Deletion & contractual mechanisms:
   - DPA: Our standard DPA (with SCCs) supports deletion obligations and data subject request handling.
   - Deletion API: We provide a programmatic deletion endpoint and a 48–72 hour SLA for bulk deletions under enterprise contracts.

4) Evidence and assessments:
   - SOC 2 Type II: summary attached (Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf). Full report available under NDA.
   - DPIA/AI assessment: summary attached (DPIA_AI_Processing_Summary.pdf) — includes risk categories, mitigation controls (redaction, sandboxing, access controls), and pseudonymization practices.
   - Retention policy: attached (Redwood_Data_Retention_v1.2.pdf) with configurable controls.

5) Additional controls worth noting:
   - KMS/HSM integration for key management (customer-managed KMS available for Private).
   - Role-based access control + audit logging + customer isolation options.
   - Governance: we log and retain records of any model-improvement opt-ins and maintain documented approval flows.

Next steps: If you want the completed SIG rows, indicate which control families you need and the redaction level. We can also arrange a 45-minute technical session with Marcus and Evelyn to walk through the SOC 2 mappings and the DPIA findings.

Regards,
